All hypothetical trade discussion should go here. If you have a piece of specific news regarding Yankee interest in moving or acquiring players, or interest from other teams about Yankee players, or if a trade has actually occurred, feel free to post a link. We don't need 1 post asking for opinions about getting Tulo, 1 post asking if we can move Drew, and 7 other posts with hypothetical discussions. All of those can go here.

My take on where they stand:

INFIELD - An offensive piece to shore up the bottom of the order. Drew, Gregorious, Ryan, and sometimes Headley make for a painfully bad bottom third of the order.

OUTFIELD - Not sure that we need anything here. Good management can get a lot out of what we have. Young at this point is great vs lefties, but worse than Drew against righties (.371 in 98 PA vs L/.177 in 140 PA vs R). I'd love to see him start over Beltran (.239 in 75 PA vs L/.271 in 190 PA vs R) when there's a lefty on the mound. Garrett Jones has the opposite split of Young, but with nowhere near as much upside. I think Jones stays on the bench until Beltran needs a day off, or until late in a game when Beltran is unavailable.

STARTING PITCHING - We could definitely use another starter... The Yankees are 13 of 15 in the AL for number of quality starts. That doesn't just boil down to a few blowouts - that's consistently inconsistent pitching. ERA against starters is middle of the pack, but opponents are hitting .274 against Yankee starters, good for 2nd to last in the AL - sounds like the defense is bailing out our starters. Relievers are top-5 in the AL for ERA. Imagine how much easier their job would be if they got more rest more often. Kuroda pt.2 would be tremendous.

BULLPEN - I honestly don't know what, if anything, should be done with the pen. A long reliever would be great, but something tells me there are enough so-so starters that if a starter is acquired, a middle reliever would appear somewhere. I hate to say it, but in the trio of Shreve, Betances, and Miller, one of them could be moved if there was a big enough need somewhere else. Not saying they should move one of them, but it is a surplus area that could be trimmed to serve something else.

TL;DR - Nothing needs to be done except possibly starting pitching. I expect 1 or 2 mid-season, small headline trades that Cashman has become known for. Nothing is a big enough weakness that they need to blow anything up at this point in the season.

An interior designer friend of mine recently had a hard drive disaster. I have recovery software that I used to get all her files back.

The problem I'm having right now is that I can't seem to fit everything I pulled off back on. My operating system says the disk is 1TB, however, I was able to pull 1.67 TB off. How can it be that this disk was able to hold 687 GB more than the operating system says is there!?
How can I recover 1.67 TB from a 1TB Hard Drive?
Looks like a file decompressed during the transfer.
Some file systems support compression and deduplicateion. Also your operating system might report the size wrong.

The partition, folder/directory, or files were setup to use compression. When you repaired the MFT and "got her files back", the files were still compressed. When you copy them from a compressed source to an uncompressed desitnation, the files get decompressed as they are written. If you were to compress the destination folder, then the system will decompress the data from the source drive and then compress it as it writes it to the destination drive. This puts a lot of work on the CPU during the transfer because it has to decompress the reads and compress the writes and would cause slowness during file transfers. Though, it may allow you to copy all the data within the 1TB space you see on the source.

Well, if it's a FAT file system, you copied the information that structures the partition. I think that applies to NTFS, too. Also, if you copied the entire drive, you likely copied the blocks at the beginning of the drive used to protect the data.
Did you also recover all the metadata? If so, you probably recovered bad blocks, lost chains, orphans, and deltas.

Not sure if this is Sociology or Psychology but I'm posting it here.

What is the point of life? I've heard from friends it's to be happy. If the point of life is to find happiness then how do we have order? Happiness can be found in good and bad. Why do people believe in God if your goal is to find happiness. If you believe in God often times you have to sacrifice some fun/sin/joy.

Is everyone else me? I had a thought and I kinda live by it. That everyone else is me. They all deserve as much as me and should be put in front of myself be cause they are me. Just like I would want the best for myself. This seems wrong because I am the only consciousness that I am aware of. If my goal in life is to have more good days than bad. Then I should care less about other people because they aren't a part of my consciousness and their emotions shouldn't affect mine. I shouldn't sacrifice personal joy for someone else, that's detrimental.

Is there any books or essays I can read on this type of thought process?
It all confuses me, the thought process never ends and my mind lingers on these type of questions constantly.
I'm not sure if this is the right sub, but I've got questions.

People have been writing about the meaning of life as long as they have been writing. You'll find the concept in all cultures. Sociologically, you can study groups of people to see how they share meaning throughout their own culture. You could dive into theology and study pinnacle religious texts like the Christian Bible or the Bhagavad Gita. You could take a slightly academic/logical route and place yourself in the context of western history by studying philosophers. Might want to read about existentialism, which is a type of philosophy that sees man as living in an unforgiving, godless and meaningless universe. And of course, a lot of psychology covers this topic, from Carl Jung to Carl Rodgers to Viktor Frankl.

I will cite Frankl, who recently helped me grapple with this issue. He says that the question "What is the meaning of life?" is improper. He says we must invert the question. Instead of us asking the question, we are called to answer it. Life is asking us "What is the meaning of your life?" We can choose in any way we like. This ties into the existential notion of complete freedom to act.
Awesome, I will definitely start adding to my reading list. I really like that quote from Frankl it helps me as well. I guess my questions are more philosophy than psychology. Thank you
